title: config get and automations test read the configuration source outside admission, so a non-regular source hangs them
description:
## Origin

Found while reviewing and landing <issue id="e8182bef-6941-45bc-a276-4d6e8cccae2b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-505/make-configuration-admission-bounded-validated-generation-bound-and">THE-505</issue> (bounded, validated configuration admission). <issue id="e8182bef-6941-45bc-a276-4d6e8cccae2b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-505/make-configuration-admission-bounded-validated-generation-bound-and">THE-505</issue>'s own commit message says it gates "startup, CLI, reload, hydration and daemon on admission" — but two CLI commands still reach the configuration source directly.

## Measured

A FIFO is used as the configuration source (`mkfifo config/blocking.toml`, `--config` pointed at it) with no writer, so anything that *opens* it blocks and anything that goes through admission refuses it as a non-regular file:

| command | behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| `thegn --version` (static) | exits 0 — never consults the source. Correct. |
| `thegn api call worktrees.list` | exits 1: `configuration refused: configuration source capture failed: configuration source is not a regular file`. **Admitted.** |
| `thegn config get drawer.height` | **blocks on the FIFO** — opens the source outside admission. |
| `thegn automations test missing --event '{}'` | **blocks on the FIFO** — same. |

So admission is not uniform across configured CLI commands.

## Why it matters

Modest but real:

* **A hang vector.** A non-regular or never-written configuration source wedges these two commands indefinitely instead of producing <issue id="e8182bef-6941-45bc-a276-4d6e8cccae2b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-505/make-configuration-admission-bounded-validated-generation-bound-and">THE-505</issue>'s bounded refusal. The whole point of the capture layer is that a bad source fails fast with an explanation.
* **Inconsistent contract.** `api call` and `config get` disagree about whether a configuration source is admissible, so `thegn config get` cannot be trusted to report the configuration the rest of the binary would actually run with — which is close to the opposite of what that command is for.
* It means the admission boundary has at least two doors, and only one is guarded. Any future reader will reasonably assume a single seam.

No security boundary is crossed: the source is supplied by the invoking user, so this is a self-inflicted hang rather than an escalation.

## Suggested fix

Route `config get` and `automations test` through the same admitted capture as `api call`, so every command that consults configuration observes one admitted generation. Then audit for any remaining direct reader — a grep for the loader entry points rather than a guess, since this issue exists because two were missed.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `config get` and `automations test` refuse a non-regular configuration source with <issue id="e8182bef-6941-45bc-a276-4d6e8cccae2b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-505/make-configuration-admission-bounded-validated-generation-bound-and">THE-505</issue>'s bounded refusal instead of blocking.
- [ ] Every CLI command that consults configuration goes through the admitted capture; static commands still never consult it.
- [ ] A test proves no configured command can block on an unread FIFO source.
- [ ] `crates/thegn-host/tests/static_cli_support/unix.rs` asserts one uniform outcome for the configured group, replacing the split assertion that this issue's discovery forced.

## Note on the test

`static_commands_do_not_open_fifo_configuration_but_configured_siblings_do` previously asserted that all three configured commands **block** on the FIFO, using that as proof they read configuration. <issue id="e8182bef-6941-45bc-a276-4d6e8cccae2b" href="https://linear.app/blakeashley/issue/THE-505/make-configuration-admission-bounded-validated-generation-bound-and">THE-505</issue> made `api call` refuse instead, so the test now asserts per-command behaviour — refusal for `api call`, blocking for the other two — with a pointer to this issue. When this lands, collapse it back to one uniform assertion.
